subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT allowed under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dual citizenship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955 governs the acquisition, determination, and termination of Indian citizenship.
 
• India does not allow **dual citizenship**. A citizen of India cannot hold citizenship of another country simultaneously.
 
• The Act provides for citizenship through five modes: **birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory**.
 
• Dual citizenship is not permitted because India follows a policy of single citizenship, ensuring uniform national identity and allegiance.
 
• Indian citizens acquiring foreign citizenship must renounce their Indian citizenship as per the provisions of the Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Naturalization:**

 
 
• Naturalization is a mode of acquiring citizenship for foreign nationals who fulfill eligibility criteria like residence in India for a specified period and good character.
 
• Applicants must renounce their citizenship of another country to become Indian citizens.
 
 
 
• **Descent-based Citizenship:**
 
 
• A person born outside India is considered an Indian citizen by descent if either of their parents is an Indian citizen.
 
• Specific conditions apply based on the date of birth and registration requirements under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
 
 
• **Registration:**
 
 
• Citizenship through registration is available for individuals like persons of Indian origin or spouses of Indian citizens who meet prescribed conditions.
 
• They must reside in India for a specific period before applying for registration.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI):**
 
 
• Though dual citizenship is not allowed, the government offers the **OCI scheme** for people of Indian origin who are citizens of other countries.
 
• OCI status provides several rights but does not equate to full citizenship, such as voting rights or eligibility for government jobs.
 
 
 
• **Renunciation and Termination of Citizenship:**
 
 
• Citizenship can be renounced voluntarily by individuals or terminated by the government in case of fraud or disloyalty.
 
• The Act specifies detailed procedures for renunciation and termination to ensure compliance with legal frameworks.
